answer.recommendation:
Channel calendar (launch February 10; year not specified in the packet, so dates are shown as month/day). Sequence the overview first for orientation, then the demo for hands-on evaluation.

- Feb 6 (T-4), Social: Teaser post introducing the overview's main value points, linking to the web overview page (which goes live at launch). Keep copy plain and jargon-light.
- Feb 9 (T-1), Email: Preview email to the subscriber list with the overview summary and a 'launching tomorrow' note. Keep to one primary link.
- Feb 10 (Launch day), Web: Publish the overview page and embed the demo on the same page, so visitors can read and watch in one place.
- Feb 10 (Launch day), Email: Launch announcement with the overview summary and a link to the demo.
- Feb 10 (Launch day), Social: Launch post with a short demo clip or screenshot linking to the web page.
- Feb 13 (T+3), Social: Repost of the demo with a single practical use case and a link to the web page.
- Feb 17 (T+7), Email: Follow-up to recipients who opened the launch email but did not click, featuring the demo directly.

Audience: the packet does not name a target audience, so this assumes a general professional audience that needs a clear overview before a demo. Confirm the audience before publishing; if it is more technical or more expert, the copy can be adjusted without changing the sequence.
quality_notes: The packet gives no year, so dates are relative to the February 10 launch (month/day only).
Target audience is not stated in the packet; the calendar assumes a general professional audience and should be confirmed.
Sequencing introduces the overview before the demo, which suits a readers-first audience with a demo for follow-up engagement.
Each channel has at least one touchpoint for each asset, and the web page is the single destination for both assets to keep links consistent.
No colleague was contacted; no approvals or audience facts were claimed beyond the packet.
Baseline summary is reproduced exactly as supplied.
